thesis: The screen behaves like a hand-bound book — warm ground, ink-black text, red seal as the only accent
reference_world: Woodblock-printed genealogies, seal script, hand-bound folios
colour_character: Warm off-white ground, ink black, one cinnabar red, aged-paper mid-tones
type_character: Serif with brush-derived contrast for headings, humanist sans for body
texture: Fine paper grain, subtle ink bleed at heading edges
best_for: Genealogy, archives, literary and ceremonial products, print crossover
cost: Photographs sit awkwardly on warm ground; needs a defined frame treatment

thesis: Depth through darkness — near-black lacquer ground with gold and vermilion emerging from it
reference_world: Vietnamese sơn mài lacquerware, temple interiors, gilded ancestral tablets
colour_character: Deep lacquer brown-black, gold, vermilion, mother-of-pearl pale
type_character: High-contrast serif display, restrained sans body
texture: Lacquer sheen gradients, fine gold rule lines
best_for: Ceremonial surfaces, hero moments, annual publications
cost: Dark-only is hostile to long reading and to projectors in bright halls

thesis: Everyday dignity — indigo cloth, whitewash and terracotta; humble rather than imperial
reference_world: Indigo-dyed cloth, whitewashed courtyard walls, terracotta roof tile
type_character: Slab or sturdy humanist serif, generous body sans
texture: Woven cloth texture, uneven whitewash edge
cost: Reads folk-craft; can undercut authority if the product must feel official

thesis: Permanence — carved text on stone, deep shadow, almost no colour
reference_world: Văn bia stone steles, temple inscriptions, rubbings
colour_character: Stone grey range, charcoal, one moss green or rust accent
type_character: Carved-letterform serif, wide tracking on headings
texture: Stone grain, rubbing texture, deep incised shadow
best_for: Memorial sections, records meant to feel permanent
cost: Very low colour range makes state encoding hard; needs shape cues

thesis: The content is the design — strong typographic hierarchy, hairline rules, almost no colour
reference_world: Broadsheet newspapers, academic journals, printed annual reports
colour_character: Paper white, ink black, one accent used sparingly
type_character: Serif headline, serif or sans body, tabular numerals
best_for: Long-form narrative, reports, dense record pages
cost: Can read as austere; needs photography or the tree to carry warmth

thesis: Everything is catalogued — visible structure, labels, reference numbers, monospaced metadata
reference_world: Library catalogues, museum accession labels, archival finding aids
colour_character: Neutral greys, one archival ochre, muted semantic set
type_character: Sans for content, monospace for identifiers and dates
best_for: Data-heavy products, search-first interfaces, verification workflows
cost: Feels clinical; hard to make emotionally warm for family or memorial content

thesis: Restraint with body heat — spacious, few elements, warm neutrals instead of cold grey
reference_world: Contemporary Japanese product design, warm-neutral editorial sites
colour_character: Warm neutral scale, one deep accent, near-black text
type_character: Single humanist sans with a real weight range
best_for: Broad-audience products, mixed young and old users
cost: Easy to reach and easy to be forgettable; the accent must be brave

thesis: Confidence through system — visible grid, strong alignment, colour used as information only
reference_world: Swiss typographic design, transit and wayfinding systems
colour_character: Neutral base with a functional colour set carrying meaning
type_character: Grotesque sans, tight scale, few weights
best_for: Dashboards, admin tools, anything where colour must mean something
cost: Cold for memorial or family content; carries no cultural voice

thesis: The visualisation is the identity — the tree or map defines colour, line weight and motion; UI recedes
colour_character: Base neutral plus a graded generational or temporal scale
type_character: Compact sans with excellent small-size legibility
texture: None on the canvas; texture only at page edges
best_for: Products whose core object is a graph, tree, or map
cost: Requires the visualisation to be finished first; chicken-and-egg risk

thesis: Built around annual ritual — the ordinary state is quiet, the ceremonial state is luminous
reference_world: Lantern festivals, altar candlelight, seasonal ritual
colour_character: Muted base, luminous warm accent reserved for ceremonial moments
type_character: Serif display for ceremonial, plain sans for everyday
texture: Soft light bloom, restricted to ceremonial surfaces
best_for: Products with a strong annual rhythm — anniversaries, memorial days
cost: Two modes double the design and testing work
